# Laptop setup guide

Please install the following programs on your laptop before the course:

- a program to log in to the cluster and copy files (Windows only, see below)
- ChimeraX 1.12 with the ArtiaX plugin
- 3dmod, the viewer from IMOD

You need a laptop on which you can install software. Choose your operating
system below.

::: {.callout-note}
## Problems with the installation?

Contact Gerrit Timpert at
[gerrit.timpert@scilifelab.se](mailto:gerrit.timpert@scilifelab.se).
If needed, we can also solve it together in a short Zoom call before the
course.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Windows

### 1. MobaXterm (cluster login and files)

MobaXterm logs in to the cluster and shows the cluster's files in a sidebar,
where you can download them. The free Home Edition is enough.

1. Open the [MobaXterm download page](https://mobaxterm.mobatek.net/download.html)
   and click **Download now** under **Home Edition**.

   ![](img/setup/win-moba-download.webp){width=700}

2. Click **Installer edition**.

   ![](img/setup/win-moba-edition.webp){width=700}

3. Unzip the downloaded file and run the installer in it with the default
   settings.

4. Start MobaXterm and click **Session**.

   ![](img/setup/win-moba-start.webp){width=700}

5. Click **SSH**.

   ![](img/setup/win-moba-session-type.png){width=700}

6. Enter `login.cryoem.se` as **Remote host** and your course user name as
   **Username**. Click **OK**.

   ![](img/setup/win-moba-ssh-settings.png){width=700}

7. The first time you connect, MobaXterm asks whether you trust the server.
   Click **Accept**.

   ![](img/setup/win-moba-hostkey.png){width=500}

8. Type your password and press Enter. The password is not shown while you
   type.

   ![](img/setup/win-moba-password.webp){width=700}

9. After the login, the sidebar on the left shows your files on the cluster.
   To copy a file to your laptop, right-click it and choose **Download**.

   ![](img/setup/win-moba-sftp-download.webp){width=700}

MobaXterm saves the session in the sidebar. Next time, double-click it to
log in again.

### 2. ChimeraX 1.12 with ArtiaX

1. Open the [ChimeraX download page](https://www.cgl.ucsf.edu/chimerax/download.html).
   Under the heading **ChimeraX 1.12**, click `ChimeraX-1.12.exe`.
   Do not take the release candidate or the daily build at the top of the
   page: ArtiaX does not work with them.

   ![](img/setup/win-chimerax-download.webp){width=700}

2. Run the installer with the default settings.

3. Start ChimeraX. Click into the field next to **Command:** at the bottom of
   the window, type `toolshed install ArtiaX` and press Enter. The log shows
   "Installed ChimeraX-ArtiaX". If orange warnings about numpy appear above
   it, you can ignore them.

   ![](img/setup/win-chimerax-artiax-install.webp){width=700}

4. In the same field, type `pip install pandas==3.0.5` and press Enter. The
   log shows no message for this command. That is normal.

   ![](img/setup/win-chimerax-pandas.webp){width=700}

   ::: {.callout-note}
   ## Why this step?

   The current ArtiaX release installs a pandas version that does not work
   with ChimeraX 1.12, so ArtiaX does not start. This step installs a version
   that works.
   :::

5. Quit ChimeraX (**File**, **Quit**) and start it again.

6. Click the **ArtiaX** tab at the top, then **Launch**.

   ![](img/setup/win-chimerax-artiax-tab.webp){width=700}

7. The ArtiaX panel opens. ChimeraX and ArtiaX are ready.

   ![](img/setup/win-chimerax-artiax-open.webp){width=700}

### 3. 3dmod

::: {.callout-important}
## Already have IMOD?

If the full IMOD is already installed on your laptop, the standalone 3dmod
does not start. Use the 3dmod from your IMOD installation and skip this part.
:::

On Windows you only need 3dmod, not the full IMOD. 3dmod is available as a
standalone package.

1. Open the [3dmod download folder](https://bio3d.colorado.edu/ftp/Windows3dmod/)
   and click `3dmodForWin64-5.2.7.exe`.

   ![](img/setup/win-3dmod-download.png){width=600}

2. Double-click the downloaded file. Keep the destination folder
   `C:\Program Files` and click **Extract**.

   ![](img/setup/win-3dmod-extract.png){width=600}

   If Windows shows a blue warning, click **More info** and then
   **Run anyway**. If Windows asks for administrator rights, right-click the
   file and choose **Run as administrator**.

3. Open the folder `C:\Program Files\3dmod`.

   ![](img/setup/win-3dmod-folder.png){width=700}

4. Right-click **3dmod** and choose **Send to**, **Desktop (create shortcut)**.
   On Windows 11, you may first have to click **Show more options**.

   ![](img/setup/win-3dmod-shortcut.webp){width=700}

5. Start 3dmod from the desktop shortcut. In the window "3dmod Startup",
   click **Select...** next to **Image file(s)**, choose a file and click
   **OK**.

   ![](img/setup/win-3dmod-startup.webp){width=700}

6. To test it, download
   [golgi.mrc](https://bio3d.colorado.edu/ftp/Windows3dmod/golgi.mrc) and
   open it. 3dmod shows the image, and its info window shows "3dmod 5.2.7".

   ![](img/setup/win-3dmod-open.webp){width=700}

## macOS

The screenshots show a Mac with Apple Silicon (M1, M2, ...).

### 1. Cluster login and files

Nothing to install. Open the app **Terminal** (in Applications, Utilities).

1. To log in, type the following and press Enter. Use your course user name
   instead of `<user>`.

   ```bash
   ssh <user>@login.cryoem.se
   ```

   ![](img/setup/mac-ssh.png){width=600}

2. The first time you connect, the Terminal asks whether you want to continue
   connecting. Type `yes` and press Enter. Then type your password and press
   Enter. The password is not shown while you type. After the login, the
   prompt shows your user name and `login1`.

   ![](img/setup/mac-ssh-login.png){width=600}

3. To log out, type `exit`. To copy a file from the cluster to your laptop,
   use `scp` in a Terminal on your laptop (not on the cluster):

   ```bash
   scp <user>@login.cryoem.se:<path on the cluster> ~/Downloads/
   ```

### 2. IMOD (3dmod)

IMOD needs Python on the Mac.

1. In the Terminal, type `python3 --version` and press Enter. If it shows a
   version number, Python is installed and you can go on with step 2.

   ![](img/setup/mac-python-check.png){width=600}

   If it shows an error or asks to install developer tools, install Python
   first: the [IMOD download page](https://bio3d.colorado.edu/imod/download.html)
   links the Python 3.10 installer from python.org in its Mac section.

2. Open the [IMOD download page](https://bio3d.colorado.edu/imod/download.html)
   and go to **Latest Stable Release Packages - Mac**. For a Mac with Apple
   Silicon, click **clickable installer** in the line
   **Mac OS 12 - 27 for arm64 processor**. For an Intel Mac, use the line
   **for Intel processor**.

   ![](img/setup/mac-imod-download.png){width=700}

3. Double-click the downloaded `.pkg` file and follow the installer with the
   default settings. It asks for your Mac password.

   ![](img/setup/mac-imod-install-done.png){width=500}

4. Close the Terminal and open a new one. The new Terminal knows where IMOD
   is. Type `which 3dmod`: it shows `/Applications/IMOD/bin/3dmod`.

   ![](img/setup/mac-imod-which.png){width=600}

5. Type `3dmod` and press Enter. In the window "3dmod Startup", click
   **Select...** next to **Image file(s)**, choose a file and click **OK**.
   Do not use the 3dmod icon in Launchpad: it does not work.

   ![](img/setup/mac-3dmod-startup.png){width=700}

6. To test it, download
   [golgi.mrc](https://bio3d.colorado.edu/ftp/Windows3dmod/golgi.mrc) and
   open it. 3dmod shows the image.

   ![](img/setup/mac-3dmod-open.png){width=700}

### 3. ChimeraX 1.12 with ArtiaX

1. Open the [ChimeraX download page](https://www.cgl.ucsf.edu/chimerax/download.html).
   Under the heading **ChimeraX 1.12**, click `ChimeraX-1.12.dmg`. For an
   Intel Mac, click **Other platforms** below it. Do not take the release
   candidate or the daily build: ArtiaX does not work with them.

   ![](img/setup/mac-chimerax-download.png){width=700}

2. Open the `.dmg` file and drag **ChimeraX-1.12** to **Applications**.

   ![](img/setup/mac-chimerax-dmg.png){width=600}

3. Start ChimeraX from Applications. The first start shows a registration
   form. You can fill it in or close it.

   ![](img/setup/mac-chimerax-register.png){width=500}

4. Click into the field next to **Command:** at the bottom of the window,
   type `toolshed install ArtiaX` and press Enter. The log shows
   "Installed ChimeraX-ArtiaX". Orange warnings about numpy above it are
   normal and can be ignored.

   ![](img/setup/mac-chimerax-artiax-install.png){width=700}

5. In the same field, type `pip install pandas==3.0.5` and press Enter. The
   log shows no message for this command. That is normal.

   ![](img/setup/mac-chimerax-pandas.png){width=700}

   ::: {.callout-note}
   ## Why this step?

   The current ArtiaX release installs a pandas version that does not work
   with ChimeraX 1.12, so ArtiaX does not start. This step installs a version
   that works.
   :::

6. Quit ChimeraX (**ChimeraX**, **Quit ChimeraX**) and start it again.

7. Click the **ArtiaX** tab at the top, then **Launch**.

   ![](img/setup/mac-chimerax-artiax-tab.png){width=700}

8. The ArtiaX panel opens. ChimeraX and ArtiaX are ready.

   ![](img/setup/mac-chimerax-artiax-open.png){width=700}

## Linux

### 1. Cluster login and files

Nothing to install. In a terminal, use `ssh` to log in and `scp` to copy
files:

```bash
ssh <user>@login.cryoem.se
```

```bash
scp <user>@login.cryoem.se:<path on the cluster> .
```

### 2. ChimeraX 1.12 with ArtiaX

1. Download ChimeraX 1.12 for your distribution from the
   [ChimeraX download page](https://www.cgl.ucsf.edu/chimerax/download.html)
   (heading **ChimeraX 1.12**, under **Other platforms**) and install it.
2. Follow steps 3 to 7 of the Windows instructions: `toolshed install ArtiaX`,
   then `pip install pandas==3.0.5`, restart ChimeraX, then **ArtiaX**,
   **Launch**.

### 3. IMOD

Install IMOD 5.x with the installer for Linux from the
[IMOD download page](https://bio3d.colorado.edu/imod/download.html) and
follow its instructions. Afterwards, open a new terminal and run `3dmod`.
